_help: Honey trees (Diamond / Pearl / Platinum). Read by js/where.js and js/maps.js. 'map' = the map id in maps.json the trees are drawn on. 'games' = games that have honey trees. 'encounters' = what a slathered tree can attract (n = national dex number, g = games, lo/hi = level range, chance = % on a normal tree). 'spots' = the 21 trees, in the numbered order of the HoneyTree sketch: 'name' is shown in the list, 'desc' is the short help text, 'boxes' = [[x,y,w,h],...] in map pixels (each tree is one 7x7 tile). To move a tree, edit its box (or use map-editor.html). Instead of 'boxes' a spot may use 'area' = an existing place name in maps.json 'areas' whose boxes are borrowed (boxes wins). In where.js these spots REPLACE the per-route 'honey-tree' rows that locations.json (PokeAPI) has for each Pokemon: the Honey Trees row is now the only place honey trees are listed.
intro: Slather Honey on a honey tree (a special tree with a different look from normal trees), then come back about 6 real-life hours later: a wild Pokémon will be on it for roughly 24 hours. Every tree gives the same Pokémon, so use whichever is closest. Rates shown are for a normal tree. Each flashing square on the map is one tree; its position is approximate (within about a tile).

notes.446: Only 4 of the 21 trees can ever attract Munchlax (about 1% each time). Which 4 depends on your Trainer ID and Secret ID, so it is different for every save file. If a tree shakes a lot when you slather it, it is more likely to be a rare Pokémon.
notes.214: Heracross is rare on every tree (about 1%). Trees that can attract Munchlax also give rare Pokémon like this more often.
